---
title: "1-D Array Benchmarks"
---

Recorded **2026-09-08**, reducers **0.4.0 + overflow fix (`eb27fc0`)**.
[Environment and setup](../performance.qmd#recorded-environment) ·
[Complete output](results/2026-09-08/one-d.txt) ·
[Excluded baselines](results/2026-09-08/one-d-exclusions.txt)

```bash
uv run --no-sync python benchmarks/benchmark_1d.py --repeats 15 --warmups 3
```

Times are median microseconds per call over 15 samples after 3 warmups;
the lowest and highest samples are discarded. Short inputs batch repeated
calls using `max(1, min(100000, 1000000 // length))` calls per sample.
Ratios above 1 favor reducers; bold means a ratio above 0.95 (within 5%).
`-` means unavailable; `n/a` means the baseline failed the accuracy check.
Ratios use unrounded times.

Inputs are prebuilt contiguous arrays; reducers uses `validate=False`.
Weights are uniform on `[0.5, 1.5)`. `var` uses `ddof=0`, `std` uses `ddof=1`.
Percentile requests `[16, 50, 84]`; quantile requests `[0.16, 0.50, 0.84]`.
NaN-aware inputs contain sparse NaNs. For NumPy `nanaverage`, the validity
mask is prepared before timing; selecting values and weights is timed.
